title: Bob Dylan Meets the Pope
summary: Bob Dylan met the pope on Wednesday. The famous American singer visited Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican in Rome. Dylan was in Italy for concerts. The meeting was short. Pope Leo gave Dylan a rosary. Dylan gave the pope a copy of his book, "Chronicles: Volume One." The two men already had a link. Pope Leo quoted one of Dylan's songs in his 2026 book about peace. The song, "Go Away You Bomb," was written by Dylan in 1963 and never released. In his book, Leo warned against building more weapons and using nuclear bombs. Dylan met the pope in private for a few minutes. He wore a black hoodie and a loose tie, with the hood up in the photos. Dylan won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 2016. This was not his first meeting with a pope. He played for Pope John Paul II in 1997 in Bologna, Italy. In 2022, he told the Wall Street Journal that he was a "religious person" who reads holy books, meditates and prays.
why_it_matters: Music can bring very different people together, even a famous singer and the pope.
